Specifically: RTO and RPO commitments by deployment mode (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private), multi-region failover sequencing (control plane vs data plane), cache/KV behavior for in-flight sessions, expected impact on latency during failover, and what evidence you can provide (runbook excerpts, test reports, RTO/RPO matrices).

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise summary and I'm attaching two artifacts to start (RTO/RPO matrix + a short runbook excerpt). Marissa and Jonas are looped in for technical/operations details and to propose a validation cadence.

Quick summary (high level):
- Hosted API: operational switchover for request routing (control-plane) — automated regional failover typically completes in 90–180 seconds for new connections; in-flight tokenized sessions may see partial state loss if KV cache cannot be replicated; expected customer-visible RTO (session continuity) range: 30s–5min depending on model size and cache window.
- Dedicated: we provide region-pinned Dedicated pools. For Dedicated with active-standby across regions we commit RTO target of 5 minutes for customer-request continuity if configured with our cross-region replication option. RPO: near-zero for persisted customer artifacts (logs, billing records); ephemeral KV cache is best-effort and may be lost unless you configure our durable checkpointing.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): behavior depends on topology. With our standard Private HA blueprint (dual-site control plane + async model artifact replication) customers see RTO targets similar to Dedicated (5–15 mins) and RPO choices down to 0 with synchronous replication.

Additional notes:
- Fallbacks: we support automatic model-variant fallback (quantized/CPU variant) to preserve availability when GPU capacity is exhausted; this is policy-driven per-route.
- Traffic routing: smart routing prefers local-region endpoints and will failover to secondary region with health checks and a gradual reroute to avoid cache storms.
- Testing: we provide a runbook template for tabletop and live failovers; we recommend quarterly rehearsals for regulated workloads.

Attached: Redwood_RTO_RPO_Matrix_v3.xlsx (matrix by deployment and failure mode), regional_failover_runbook_snippet.docx (excerpt showing sequencing and ops playbook).

Next steps: Marissa/Jonas — can you add the deeper sequencing and canary/traffic-shift examples? Lena — happy to scope a short validation workshop (2 weeks) to demonstrate failover and collect artifacts for your InfoSec team.

Best,

Priyom Das

Lena / team — adding a few technical clarifications to the high-level above and a small policy example.

Technical clarifications (concise):
- Control plane vs data plane: control plane (routing, orchestration) is replicated across regions with leader-election; control-plane takeover is sub-2 minutes for management operations. Data plane (inference nodes + KV) has replication options:
  * Async model artifact replication (default) — RPO: minutes; recommended for cost-sensitive setups.
  * Synchronous checkpointing for KV and session state — RPO: near-zero; adds ~5–10% write latency.
- KV cache behavior: by default KV cache is local to the inference GPU host. For session continuity we offer two patterns: (1) periodic durable checkpoints to object storage (configurable frequency) and (2) cross-region streaming of critical keys for hot sessions. Pattern (2) gives best continuity at higher cost.
- Failover sequencing: our runbook enforces (1) degrade-to-quantized-variant policy, (2) route new traffic to secondary region, (3) probe model warmup, (4) incrementally drain and route. This reduces cold-start amplification.

Canary policy example attached — shows a 5–20% traffic ramp over 10 minutes with health checks and automatic rollback on model error rate increase.

Attachment: canary_policy_examples.pdf

I'll follow up with a short checklist for your compliance team (SOC2 evidence pointers, logs, retention windows).

— Marissa
